items.question: Rule the Jer.49.19|Jer.49.20 cut question (peer: any change to the span, including adopting that cut, is a PROPOSAL for adoption). ADOPT with exact spec, or DECLINE. Note the cross-lens factual tension the primaries recorded over what pmarks carries at 49:19 - arbitrate against the inventory bytes.

P18-006.challenge_claim: Two convergent items. (1) The front seam at Jer.49.19 rests on a fresh poetic image alone: no tier-1 device stands at the onset and no parashah mark falls at the Jer.49.18|Jer.49.19 edge, and the medium confidence never engages that gap. (2) The stated grammatical ground for not cutting at the setumah recorded at MT 49:19 -- that the lion simile's rhetorical questions run past the verse boundary into Jer.49.20-Jer.49.21 -- is contradicted by the verse bytes.
P18-006.grounds: Both items verify. They are DISTINCT defects converging on one weakness: the first attacks the seam this unit draws, the second the ground on which it declines the seam inside its span. Item 1. Jer.49.19 opens הִ֠נֵּה כְּאַרְיֵ֞ה (oshb:Jer.49.19, byte tier), a presentative plus simile. The verse belongs to none of the three word-event shapes, stands among neither the six lamed-initial nation headers nor the four non-lamed header shapes, carries no koh-amar, no vocative and no imperative, and is absent from the 19 classified date-candidate sites -- so no tier-1 device stands at the onset. In the parashah layer (tier-3 weak, single-witness) the entries in and around the span are setumah keyed to MT 49:11, MT 49:19 and MT 49:22; the MT 49:19 entry trails that verse and therefore sits INSIDE the span, between its first and second verses, and nothing is keyed to MT 49:18, so the front edge carries no mark either. observed_substrate_signals records a refrain key only, which under the ruled granularity is texture, not an onset class. Item 2. The question series terminates inside Jer.49.19: וּמִי זֶ֣ה רֹעֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָֽי (oshb:Jer.49.19, byte tier) closes at the verse-final accent, and Jer.49.20 opens לָכֵ֞ן שִׁמְע֣וּ (oshb:Jer.49.20, byte tier) -- a consequential particle plus second-person-plural imperative beginning an independent clause, the voice turning from first-person divine speech to speech about Yahweh in the third person. The second witness agrees, closing its quotation at the end of the verse and carrying “Therefore hear the counsel of Yahweh, that he has taken against Edom” (web:Jer.49.20) outside it. The sentence-continuation ground is byte-false at both witnesses. NEW FINDING, which inverts the two items against each other: the seam this unit declines at Jer.49.19|Jer.49.20 carries a hear-imperative of the same shape the ruled granularity names as a tier-1 internal seam class, plus the tier-3 setumah, while the seam it draws at Jer.49.18|Jer.49.19 carries neither. The disposition can still survive, but only on the ground the unit already holds elsewhere: the same two-verse template stands at Jer.49.19-Jer.49.20 and at Jer.50.44-Jer.50.45, and this tiling reads Jer.50.44-Jer.50.46 as one unit, so cutting at Jer.49.19|Jer.49.20 would force the parallel cut there. SECOND NEW FINDING, on the recurrence digits: the leading identical run is 9 whitespace tokens at Jer.49.19 against Jer.50.44 (byte tier; diverging at the tenth, plene against defective, with a variant note carried at MT 50:44 and none at MT 49:19) and 7 whitespace tokens at Jer.49.20 against Jer.50.45 (byte tier; diverging at the nation name), counted on the maqaf-free staged extract -- the challenge's 7 and 6 name the right object under a maqaf-joined unit and understate it. THIRD NEW FINDING: both parashah citations here carry neither the single-witness nor the tier-3 label the Prophets rule requires on every citation.
P18-006.remedy: boundary_rationale: delete the clause asserting that the lion simile's rhetorical questions continue grammatically past Jer.49.19 into Jer.49.20-Jer.49.21, and delete the matching clause in strongest_rejected_alternative asserting that the sentence the mark falls inside continues past the verse boundary; both are byte-false. Replace the warrant with the parallel-treatment ground the unit already carries, stated with its tier and unit: the same template opens Jer.49.19-Jer.49.20 and Jer.50.44-Jer.50.45, byte-identical for the leading 9 and 7 whitespace tokens respectively, and this tiling reads Jer.50.44-Jer.50.46 as one unit. In boundary_rationale, disclose that no tier-1 device stands at Jer.49.19 and that no parashah entry is keyed to MT 49:18, and add the single-witness and tier-3 labels to both parashah citations. Re-rate confidence against that disclosure. CURE TEST: the rewritten boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative must survive a read of Jer.49.19 and Jer.49.20 side by side -- the sentence-continuation claim that failed must not reappear in any form, and the restated warrant must apply symmetrically at Jer.50.44|Jer.50.45. Any change to the span itself, including adopting the Jer.49.19|Jer.49.20 cut, is a PROPOSAL for owner adoption, not author work.

row.boundary_rationale: A fresh simile opens the row: “Behold, he will come up like a lion from the pride of the Jordan” (web:Jer.49.19), spliced הִ֠נֵּה כְּאַרְיֵ֞ה יַעֲלֶ֨ה מִגְּא֣וֹן הַיַּרְדֵּן֮ אֶל נְוֵ֣ה אֵיתָן֒ (oshb:Jer.49.19, byte tier), running through the rhetorical questions “who is like me?” to a therefore-clause at 49:20, “hear the counsel of Yahweh, that he has taken against Edom”, rendering לָכֵ֞ן שִׁמְע֣וּ עֲצַת יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָעַץ֙ אֶל אֱד֔וֹם (oshb:Jer.49.20, byte tier). The row closes with a second predator image at 49:22, the eagle spreading its wings over Bozrah, and the heart-of-a-woman-in-pangs simile ending the Edom oracle. A setumah falls mid-span at Jer.49.19, this row's own opening verse, and a further setumah closes the row at Jer.49.22; the mid-span mark is disclosed rather than treated as a required cut, since the lion simile's rhetorical questions continue grammatically past 49:19 into 49:20-21, and the same lion-from-the-Jordan template is read as one unit again at Jer.50.44-46, arguing for parallel treatment here.
row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at the Jer.49.19 setumah, isolating the lion simile from the counsel-and-trembling material that follows it, was considered: the mark is real but the sentence it falls inside continues past the verse boundary, and this tiling reads the whole poem as one unit.
row.literature_type_guess: lion-simile judgment poem closing the Edom oracle with an eagle image over Bozrah

row.device_notes: The lion-from-the-Jordan template (hinneh ke'aryeh ya'aleh migge'on hayarden) and the therefore-hear-the-counsel line that follows it are read again at Jer.50.44-45 for Babylon, a shared compositional template disclosed as texture across the two oracles.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The voice shifts from Yahweh's own oath to the prophet's report of what he has heard: “I have heard news from Yahweh” (web:Jer.49.14), spliced שְׁמוּעָ֤ה שָׁמַ֨עְתִּי֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.49.14, byte tier) -- shmuah shama'ti me'et YHWH, a first-person prophetic frame distinct in grammatical subject from the divine oath just closed, reporting a summons to battle against Edom. The address returns to direct second-person indictment at 49:16, “the pride of your heart has deceived you,” closing “I will bring you down from there” (web:Jer.49.16), the source's own closing quote falling before its “says Yahweh” tag. The row runs through the astonishment notice (49:17) to the Sodom-and-Gomorrah comparison closing 49:18: “no man will dwell there, neither will any son of man live therein” (web:Jer.49.18), spliced לֹֽא יֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא יָג֥וּר בָּ֖הּ בֶּן אָדָֽם (oshb:Jer.49.18, byte tier).
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Opening a fresh row at 49:17's astonishment notice, separating it from the prophet's own battle-report, was considered: 49:14-18 reads as one sustained movement from the heard summons to its Sodom-and-Gomorrah verdict, without a further addressee shift strong enough to cut inside it.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: prophetic battle-report opening into a terror indictment and a Sodom-Gomorrah verdict

prev_row.device_notes: The closing clause here (lo yeshev sham ish velo yagur bah ben adam) recurs byte-identically at Jer.49.33 (closing the Hazor oracle) and at Jer.50.40 (closing a Babylon desolation unit) -- a shared refrain disclosed as cross-reference texture, not claimed as evidence of how widely the idiom recurs across the book, which is not swept beyond these sites.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A third header opens the row, but of a different shape than its neighbors: “Of Damascus” (web:Jer.49.23), spliced לְדַמֶּ֗שֶׂק בּ֤וֹשָֽׁה חֲמָת֙ וְאַרְפָּ֔ד (oshb:Jer.49.23, byte tier) -- ledammeseq boshah Chamat ve'Arpad, naming the addressed city without a koh-amar or asher-hayah formula anywhere in the unit that follows, unlike the Ammon, Edom, and Kedar headers earlier and later in this chapter. The lament over Damascus (49:23-24) and the city-of-praise question (49:25, which also carries a ketiv/qere note on the demonstrative at Jer.49.25, consulted per the inventory but not spliced here) run to a neum-tsevaot closure at 49:26, spliced נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.49.26, byte tier), “says Yahweh of Armies”, with a first-person fire-against-the-wall coda at 49:27 continuing the same divine voice past that closure. This span's own front seam is Jer.49.22 (SAMEKH), closing the Edom oracle just before it; a further setumah at Jer.49.27 closes this row.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting the row at 49:26's neum-tsevaot closure, treating 49:27's fire-against-Damascus coda as its own unit the way the Ammon restoration coda is treated at Jer.49.6, was considered: unlike that coda, 49:27 continues the same judgment content and voice rather than pivoting to restoration, so this tiling keeps it inside the Damascus row.
next_row.literature_type_guess: nation-header oracle against Damascus, lacking an internal koh-amar reintroduction

items.question: Rule the respan PROPOSAL with TWO options: (i) Jer.49.28-Jer.49.33 entire, or (ii) a cut at Jer.49.29|Jer.49.30 where the discriminators actually sit. ADOPT exactly one option with full spec + tiling, or DECLINE both.

P18-009.challenge_claim: Two convergent items. (1) The seam actually drawn at Jer.49.31|Jer.49.32 carries no device in any layer, while strongest_rejected_alternative defends a different location, Jer.49.30, which is interior to the preceding unit and is not a seam anywhere in this tiling; the high confidence engages neither gap. (2) The opening sentence's claim that the material continues without an addressee shift is contradicted at that seam, where second-person-plural imperative address gives way to third-person report.
P18-009.grounds: Both verify. They are the SAME core defect -- an unwarranted seam defended from the wrong location -- with a distinct byte finding attached to the second item. The substrate is silent at the seam: Jer.49.32 opens וְהָי֨וּ גְמַלֵּיהֶ֜ם (oshb:Jer.49.32, byte tier) -- no speech formula, no header of the lamed or non-lamed class, no word-event shape, no date element, no vocative, no imperative; no parashah entry falls between the setumah keyed to MT 49:27 and the setumah keyed to MT 49:33; and no variant note and no paseq seg falls at MT 49:31 or MT 49:32. The rejected alternative's two discriminators -- the change of named target to Hazor and the renewed flight command -- both stand at Jer.49.30, interior to Jer.49.28-Jer.49.31, so the field's warrant addresses a boundary this tiling does not draw while the boundary it does draw is left unwarranted. The distinct byte finding: Jer.49.31 opens ק֣וּמוּ עֲל֗וּ (oshb:Jer.49.31, byte tier) against ק֚וּמוּ עֲל֣וּ (oshb:Jer.49.28, byte tier) -- direct second-person-plural imperative address bracketing Jer.49.28-Jer.49.31 -- and Jer.49.32 drops that address for third-person report closing on the divine formula. NEW FINDING, a tier correction on that comparandum: each splice is byte tier at its own verse, but the RECURRENCE between them is accent_stripped and skeleton tier, not byte -- the two accent patterns differ -- so the bracket must be cited at the tier it actually reaches. On either available reading -- an undisclosed change of address at the seam, or no device at the seam at all -- the opening sentence is false and a high confidence rating with frontier_flag_considered false cannot stand.
P18-009.remedy: boundary_rationale: strike 'The spoils continue without an addressee shift' -- the imperative address standing at Jer.49.31 does not continue into Jer.49.32 -- and state what, if anything, stands at Jer.49.31|Jer.49.32, disclosing that no tier-1 device and no mark-layer entry falls there. strongest_rejected_alternative: rewrite so its warrant addresses the seam actually drawn; a discriminator located at Jer.49.30 cannot license a cut at Jer.49.31|Jer.49.32. confidence: lower from high, and set frontier_flag_considered true. If the Jer.49.28|Jer.49.31 imperative bracket is cited, cite it at accent_stripped or skeleton tier, not byte. Add single-witness and tier-3 labels to the parashah citation. CURE TEST: the replacement warrant must be located AT Jer.49.31|Jer.49.32 and checkable there -- it fails if any verse other than Jer.49.31 or Jer.49.32 supplies it, which is exactly the test the original failed. Respanning -- to Jer.49.28-Jer.49.33 entire, or to a cut at Jer.49.29|Jer.49.30 where the discriminators actually sit -- is a PROPOSAL for owner adoption, not author work.

row.boundary_rationale: The spoils continue without an addressee shift: “Their camels will be a booty” (web:Jer.49.32), closing on the desolation formula at 49:33, “Hazor will be a dwelling place of jackals”, spliced וְהָיְתָ֨ה חָצ֜וֹר לִמְע֥וֹן תַּנִּ֛ים שְׁמָמָ֖ה עַד עוֹלָ֑ם (oshb:Jer.49.33, byte tier), running into the same Sodom-and-Gomorrah refrain closing the Edom row at Jer.49.18: לֹֽא יֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא יָג֥וּר בָּ֖הּ בֶּן אָדָֽם (oshb:Jer.49.33, byte tier), “No man will dwell there, neither will any son of man live therein” (web:Jer.49.33). A setumah at Jer.49.33 closes the row and the Kedar-and-Hazor oracle together.
row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping Jer.49.28-Jer.49.33 together as one six-verse row spanning the whole Kedar-and-Hazor oracle was considered: the shift in named target from Kedar (49:28-29) to Hazor (49:30-33) and the renewed flee-imperative at 49:30 are treated here as sufficient to open a fresh row before the closing spoils-and-desolation material.
row.literature_type_guess: closing spoils notice and desolation formula ending the Kedar-and-Hazor oracle
row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
row.device_notes: This verse's closing clause is byte-identical to the refrain closing the Edom row at Jer.49.18 and the Babylon-desolation row at Jer.50.40; the recurrence is disclosed as texture across the three sites, not swept for exclusivity.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The fourth lamed header opens the row: “Of Kedar, and of the kingdoms of Hazor” (web:Jer.49.28), spliced לְקֵדָ֣ר וּֽלְמַמְלְכ֣וֹת חָצ֗וֹר (oshb:Jer.49.28, byte tier). The same verse dates the coming strike to Nebuchadnezzar and carries this span's flagship ketiv/qere note on the king's own name: the ketiv writes the plene byform נבוכדראצור (oshb:Jer.49.28, byte tier), an added vav before the final resh, corrected by the qere to the dominant resh-family spelling נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר (oshb:Jer.49.28, byte tier) used at the majority of this name's occurrences elsewhere in the book; the verse also carries a paseq mark per the inventory (single-witness; unlocated within the verse). The koh-amar formula and the imperative “Arise, go up to Kedar” (web:Jer.49.28) follow in the same verse, spliced כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה ק֚וּמוּ עֲל֣וּ אֶל קֵדָ֔ר (oshb:Jer.49.28, byte tier), continuing through the spoils notice (49:29) into a second flee-command redirected at Hazor: “Flee! Wander far off! Dwell in the depths, you inhabitants of Hazor” (web:Jer.49.30), rendering נֻסוּ֩ נֻּ֨דוּ מְאֹ֜ד הֶעְמִ֧יקוּ לָשֶׁ֛בֶת יֹשְׁבֵ֥י חָצ֖וֹר (oshb:Jer.49.30, byte tier). This verse carries its own ketiv/qere note at Jer.49.30 on the preposition-plus-suffix pair, the ketiv reading "against them" corrected by the qere to "against you", consulted per the inventory but not spliced here. Jer.49.27, the fire-against-Damascus coda, closes with a setumah immediately before this row begins; the row closes at 49:31's command to go up against an easy-dwelling, gateless nation.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating 49:28 alone as its own row, separate from the imperative it opens, was considered: the header's own command, “Arise, go up to Kedar” (web:Jer.49.28), does not complete its sense without the spoils notice in 49:29, so this tiling keeps the header with its immediate development.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: dated nation-header oracle against Kedar and Hazor, carrying the king's-name textual variant
prev_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
prev_row.device_notes: Nebuchadnezzar's name carries four live spellings across this book; Jer.49.28's ketiv is the sole site of the plene resh-family byform, standing beside the dominant resh-family spelling (used elsewhere at, for example, Jer.49.30 and Jer.50.17) as a doubled token in one verse -- distinct from the nun-family spellings clustered in chapters 27-29.

next_row.boundary_rationale: The fifth and final header of this chapter opens the row in the asher-hayah OAN shape rather than the lamed-initial pattern of its neighbors: “Yahweh's word that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam” (web:Jer.49.34), spliced אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֧ה דְבַר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא אֶל עֵילָ֑ם (oshb:Jer.49.34, byte tier), dated within the same verse to “the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah”, rendering בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַלְכ֛וּת צִדְקִיָּ֥ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.49.34, byte tier) -- bereshit malkhut Tsidqiyahu, a construct distinct from the bereshit-mamlekhet date frames used elsewhere in this book's narrative chapters. A koh-amar-tsevaot onset follows immediately at 49:35, “Behold, I will break the bow of Elam”, spliced כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִנְנִ֥י שֹׁבֵ֖ר אֶת קֶ֣שֶׁת עֵילָ֑ם (oshb:Jer.49.35, byte tier), continuing through the four-winds scattering (Jer.49.36, which also carries a ketiv/qere note on "Elam" itself, consulted per the inventory but not spliced here), the dismay-and-sword declaration (Jer.49.37, which carries two paseq marks per the inventory, single-witness and unlocated within the verse), to the throne-in-Elam image closing 49:38 -- one continuous first-person divine speech about Elam with no addressee directly spoken to and no fresh formula reintroduced after 49:35. This span's front seam is Jer.49.33 (SAMEKH), closing the Kedar-and-Hazor oracle just before it opens.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the header (49:34) from the koh-amar declaration it introduces (49:35-38) was considered and set aside: the header's own dated superscription carries no content of its own apart from the judgment that immediately follows, matching how this chapter's other headers are kept with their immediate development.
next_row.literature_type_guess: dated asher-hayah header (Zedekiah's accession) opening the Elam judgment oracle
next_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
next_row.device_notes: The dating clause here (bereshit malkhut Tsidqiyahu) is read directly from the verse's own bytes and is not classified among this book's bereshit-mamlekhet sites, which use a different construct spelling in the narrative chapters; the two are named as distinct date-frame forms.

items.question: Rule the PROPOSAL: respan Jer.50.33-Jer.50.38 as one koh-amar-headed unit, absorbing this row into the one before it, as against keeping the cut with the ordered disclosures. ADOPT with exact spec + retirement + tiling, or DECLINE.

P18-026.challenge_claim: Two items converging on the row's front seam. Item one: the row opens a fresh unit at a verse carrying none of this block's licensed internal-cut signals, and its rejected alternative never engages the stronger rival of one continuous declaration from the Jer.50.33 onset. Item two: the pointed wordplay is byte-exact as argued, but a construct chain attested at three verses stands on both sides of the row's own front seam undisclosed, and the sword is described as repeated against a six-item list when two of the items hang off a prepositional chain.
P18-026.grounds: The observations are byte-true; the framing overstates what they settle. Byte-true against the row: oshb:Jer.50.35 carries no koh-amar onset, no hoy, no date frame and no vocative, and its only formula token is the mid-verse נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה, which is closure corroboration and not an onset device; its grammar is third-person description governed by a repeated prepositional chain. So none of the internal-cut devices named for this block stands at the onset, and the row's declared scene-shift signal carries the whole warrant. Compounding it, the construct chain stands at exactly 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier, verse counts, MT keys -- Jer.50.34, Jer.50.35, Jer.51.12) with לְיֹשְׁבֵ֥י בָבֶֽל closing oshb:Jer.50.34 against וְאֶל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י בָבֶ֔ל at oshb:Jer.50.35 (byte tier), a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam and disclosed at neither end. And the row's strongest_rejected_alternative engages only the split at Jer.50.38, never the continuous reading from the Jer.50.33 onset -- confirmed in the field's own text. The list looseness is byte-confirmed too: five sword tokens stand over MT 50:35-50:37 (one at 50:35, two at 50:36, two at 50:37, skeleton tier, MT keys), and the princes and wise men of 50:35 hang off that verse's single sword by the prepositional chain rather than heading their own sword clause; the row's list also drops the two objects that sword actually governs first. What holds and is not contested: the pointing claim is exact at codepoint level -- חֶ֥רֶב at oshb:Jer.50.35 against חֹ֥רֶב at oshb:Jer.50.38 share skeleton and accent and differ in the first vowel alone -- and the anaphora the rejected alternative relies on does run unbroken across 50:35-50:38; mark disclosure inside the span is complete, since no parashah mark, no paseq and no ketiv/qere note falls in MT 50:35-50:38, so nothing is owed there. Why refine rather than uphold: what the bytes settle is the disclosure gap and the un-engaged rival, not the seam. Internal stanza seams in this Babylon material are held open at a low-confidence posture rather than decided, and a boundary change is a proposal requiring explicit adoption, never author work. The corrected finding is an under-warranted and under-disclosed seam carried at too high a confidence, not a demonstrated mis-cut.
P18-026.remedy: Four author edits plus one proposal. (1) SEAM-PAIR CURE, ONE EDIT AT BOTH ENDS: device_notes -- disclose the yoshvei-Bavel construct chain straddling the Jer.50.34 | Jer.50.35 seam with its swept object, unit, digit and tier, paired with the same disclosure at the row closing at Jer.50.34. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the Jer.50.38-split rival with the stronger one -- reading the koh-amar-tsevaot declaration opening at Jer.50.33 straight through the litany as one unit -- and answer it on bytes. Test the cure must pass -- the test that killed the original -- the rival engaged must be the strongest available at this seam, not the most easily set aside. (3) boundary_rationale: re-cut the sword sentence to the bytes -- one sword token at Jer.50.35 governing the Chaldeans and, through the prepositional chain, the inhabitants of Babylon, her princes and her wise men; four further sword tokens heading their own clauses at Jer.50.36-Jer.50.37 (sweep: 5 tokens over 3 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys). (4) confidence: lower to medium_low with a bespoke rationale naming the undisclosed cross-seam chain, matching the held-open posture for internal stanza seams in this material. (5) PROPOSAL ONLY, requiring explicit boss adoption and expressly NOT author work: respan Jer.50.33-Jer.50.38 as one koh-amar-headed unit, absorbing this row into the one before it, as against keeping the cut with the disclosures above. Do not execute without adoption.

row.boundary_rationale: An anaphoric litany opens the row: “A sword is on the Chaldeans” (web:Jer.50.35), spliced חֶ֥רֶב עַל כַּשְׂדִּ֖ים (oshb:Jer.50.35, byte tier), cherev repeated against her princes, her wise men, her boasters, her mighty men, her horses and chariots, and her treasures across 50:35-37 with no addressee change. items.question: Rule the 51:26|51:27 seam itself (peer: PROPOSAL requiring explicit adoption, NOT author work). ADOPT an exact change, or DECLINE.

P19-006.challenge_claim: First challenge: the cross-seam catchword citation misidentifies the bigram that actually recurs between the two mobilization calls, and the 51:27 pairing quotes a shorter Hebrew span than the English beside it. Second challenge: the quoted pair does not stand in the verse it is attributed to, its digit belongs to an object the row never names, the stated ground for refusing a seam at 51:27 tests only for parent-level header shapes while a neighbouring unit is allowed to open on the very class denied here, and the row's remaining bounding warrant is a tier-3 mark pair while the byte-grade closure at the preceding verse goes unnamed.
P19-006.grounds: Both upheld; the catchword arm is the SAME defect in both challenges, and the warrant arms are DISTINCT additions. (1) The citation is byte-false at the site it is attributed to. The pair בָּבֶ֜ל שְׂאוּ, carried under a byte-tier label and placed against the call standing at web:Jer.51.27, re-collates at tier NONE against oshb:Jer.51.27; it reaches byte tier only at oshb:Jer.51.12, and there the first word is the nomen rectum of the phrase governing the imperative, אֶל חוֹמֹ֨ת בָּבֶ֜ל שְׂאוּ נֵ֗ס, so the pair splices across a phrase boundary and is not a call at either site (sweep at consonantal tier of that pair: 1 verse, oshb:Jer.51.12 alone). (2) The digit belongs to an unnamed object. The form the two verses actually share is שְׂאוּ נֵ֗ס at 51:12 against שְׂאוּ נֵ֣ס at 51:27 - the same two words, differing in the accent on the second, so the recurrence holds at accent_stripped tier across the pair and not at byte tier. That form sweeps at consonantal tier to 4 verses book-wide (4:6, 50:2, 51:12, 51:27), 2 of them in this chapter: the chapter digit the row cites fits an object it neither names nor quotes. (3) Gloss extent. The splice at oshb:Jer.51.27 covers the phrase the English renders “Set up a standard in the land!” (web:Jer.51.27), while the clause attached runs on through “Blow the trumpet among the nations!” (web:Jer.51.27), which renders תִּקְע֨וּ שׁוֹפָ֤ר בַּגּוֹיִם֙. (4) The not-cutting warrant tests the wrong class. oshb:Jer.51.27 opens verse-initially with a six-command imperative series addressed to the nations in the plural - the challenge's four is a miscount, and since no morphology layer is staged the count is read from the pointed bytes plus both renderings, which carry six commands each - against the singular addressee running through 51:25-26; the ground offered for holding the two halves together tests only for a divine-speech or word-event formula, which are parent-level header shapes, while verse-initial discourse imperatives are themselves an internal-seam class - the class on which an imperative-vocative opens a unit at oshb:Jer.51.45 in this same stretch. What then does the holding-together work in the row's own prose is the flanking setumah pair, tier-3 and single-witness, which cannot carry it. NEW, named by neither challenge: oshb:Jer.51.26 also closes verse-final with נְאֻם יְהוָֽה, immediately before that imperative onset - the same closure-plus-fresh-onset configuration this tiling treats as a seam one verse-pair earlier, where verse-final נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה at 51:24 is followed by the addressee shift at 51:25. The row discloses neither the closure at 51:24 nor the one at 51:26. Verified sound and not disturbed: the onset splice at oshb:Jer.51.25 re-collates at byte tier and the addressee shift there is a real tier-1 signal, and the marks at MT 51:24 and MT 51:32 are correctly typed. REFERRED, NOT DECIDED: whether that configuration cuts at 51:26|51:27 is a boundary proposal inside the deliberately held-open internal stanza policy of the Babylon complex; it needs explicit owner adoption and no respan is ordered here.
P19-006.remedy: boundary_rationale: delete the two-word catchword citation - it reaches tier none at oshb:Jer.51.27 and byte tier only at oshb:Jer.51.12, where it splices the object of a governing phrase onto the following imperative. Replace it with the form the two verses actually share, spliced separately from each site, with the cross-site tier named (accent_stripped, the two differing in one accent) and the digit re-attached to that object: sweep 4 verses book-wide - 4:6, 50:2, 51:12, 51:27 - 2 of them in this chapter. boundary_rationale: re-cut the 51:27 pairing to the splice extent or extend the splice through the trumpet clause. boundary_rationale: restate the ground for holding the two halves together in the internal-seam vocabulary rather than the parent-header vocabulary, and say why a verse-initial imperative series does not cut here when the same class opens a unit at 51:45. boundary_rationale and boundary_evidence_refs: cite the byte-grade closure standing verse-final at oshb:Jer.51.24 as the onset-side warrant, and disclose the second closure standing verse-final at oshb:Jer.51.26 immediately before the imperative onset, with the addressee number shift from singular to plural; the flanking parashah marks then stay tier-3 corroboration rather than the bounding argument. The 51:26|51:27 seam itself is a PROPOSAL requiring explicit owner adoption and is NOT author work. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: every Hebrew citation re-collates at the ref it is placed against, at the tier claimed; every digit names the object it counts and its unit; and the not-cutting warrant, applied to this stretch, must distinguish 51:27 from the verse-initial imperative onsets the same stretch does cut.

row.boundary_rationale: This row opens with a second addressee shift, oshb:Jer.51.25 (byte tier) הִנְנִ֨י אֵלֶ֜יךָ הַ֤ר הַמַּשְׁחִית֙, “Behold, I am against you, destroying mountain” (web:Jer.51.25), addressing Babylon under a fresh figure. Partway through, a discourse-imperative reopens the material at oshb:Jer.51.27 (byte tier) שְׂאוּ נֵ֣ס בָּאָ֗רֶץ, “Set up a standard in the land! Blow the trumpet among the nations!” (web:Jer.51.27), the same two-word call, בָּבֶ֜ל שְׂאוּ (byte tier), that opened the earlier mobilization at oshb:Jer.51.12 (sweep: 2 verses within this chapter). Both the mountain address and the renewed call to arms are held in one row bounded by the setumah marks on either side, given that neither shift carries a koh-amar or word-event formula of its own.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh addressee shift opens this row: oshb:Jer.51.20 (byte tier) מַפֵּץ אַתָּ֣ה לִ֔י, “You are my battle ax and weapons of war” (web:Jer.51.20), turning from the doxology’s third-person hymn to a direct second-person address to YHWH’s own instrument of conquest. The fivefold break-in-pieces refrain runs to a talionic notice closing at oshb:Jer.51.24 (byte tier) נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה, “all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight” (web:Jer.51.24), where a setumah marks the section end.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar onset carrying the full divine title stack opens this row: oshb:Jer.51.33 (byte tier) כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל, echoed in “The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor” (web:Jer.51.33) — the stacked title YHWH of Armies, the God of Israel is a recurring Jer signature (32 verses book-wide). The row then shifts to a first-person victim voice at oshb:Jer.51.34 (ketiv/qere), which opens with the doubled reading אכלנו אֲכָלַ֣נִי before naming נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֮ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶל֒, “Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon has devoured me. He has crushed me. He has made me an empty vessel” (web:Jer.51.34); the verse carries multiple ketiv/qere notes (5, per the inventory). The unit closes after Zion’s own imprecation at oshb:Jer.51.35.

items.question: Rule the proposed cut at 52:6 (peer: boundary proposal requiring explicit adoption). ADOPT with exact spec, or DECLINE.

P20-002.challenge_claim: The stated ground for holding Jer.52.4-Jer.52.11 whole - that no fresh date breaks the chain - is contested by 52:6, which opens its verse with a month-and-day dating notice in the same shape treated as boundary-bearing at 52:12.
P20-002.grounds: Byte-confirmed. Jer 52:6 opens בַּחֹ֤דֶשׁ הָֽרְבִיעִי֙ בְּתִשְׁעָ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ (oshb:Jer.52.6, byte tier): month ordinal plus day, verse-initial and asyndetic, with the famine clause following it; the span quotes and disposition nothing from that verse. The boundary drawn at Jer.52.12 rests on וּבַחֹ֤דֶשׁ הַֽחֲמִישִׁי֙ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ (oshb:Jer.52.12, byte tier) - the same month-and-day shape carrying only a prefixed vav and a mid-verse year gloss. The span does clear the weaker shape at 52:5 explicitly and correctly, עַ֚ד עַשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.52.5, byte tier) being a terminus rather than an onset, which makes the silence over the stronger verse-initial shape at 52:6 an asymmetry inside the same class rather than a uniform decision about it. The 52:6 notice carries no year word, so it is invisible to a year-token sweep - that explains the omission but does not license the categorical wording, which as written is falsified by a dating notice standing inside the span. The English paragraph break at that verse is tier-4 and carries no weight in either direction. What is upheld is the wording defect only: whether 52:6 should cut is not decided here, since its date sits inside the siege the 52:4 frame opens, and whether a yearless verse-initial month-and-day notice belongs to the ruled date-onset class is a definitional question the granularity ruling does not settle.
P20-002.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative and boundary_rationale: replace the categorical no-fresh-date wording with a per-site reading that names oshb:Jer.52.6, quotes its verse-initial month-and-day run at byte tier, and states why it is read as internal to the siege the 52:4 frame opens - the same per-site treatment the row already gives the terminus at 52:5. device_notes: name the shape and its year-word absence. boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Jer.52.6. Test the cure must pass: no categorical claim about dates survives in the row that a dating notice standing inside Jer.52.4-Jer.52.11 falsifies, and every date-shaped verse inside the span is dispositioned per-site with its bytes quoted. A cut at 52:6 is a boundary proposal requiring explicit adoption, never author work under this remedy.

row.boundary_rationale: A verse-initial date frame opens this span, וַיְהִי֩ בַשָּׁנָ֨ה הַתְּשִׁעִ֜ית לְמָלְכ֗וֹ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִי֮ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ֒ בָּ֠א נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֨ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֜ל ה֤וּא וְכָל חֵילוֹ֙ עַל יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ עָלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּבְנ֥וּ עָלֶ֛יהָ דָּיֵ֖ק סָבִֽיב (oshb:Jer.52.4, byte), matching “In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, and encamped against it; and they built forts against it round about.” (web:Jer.52.4). The siege account that follows stays one unbroken chain under this dated onset through the city's fall, the king's flight and capture in the plains of Jericho, and his being brought to Nebuchadnezzar for sentence, וַֽיִּתְפְּשׂוּ֙ אֶת הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיַּעֲל֨וּ אֹת֜וֹ אֶל מֶ֧לֶךְ בָּבֶ֛ל רִבְלָ֖תָה בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֲמָ֑ת וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ מִשְׁפָּטִֽים (oshb:Jer.52.9, byte), matching “Then they took the king, and carried him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah in the land of Hamath; and he pronounced judgment on him.” (web:Jer.52.9). The span closes on the sentence's own execution, וְאֶת עֵינֵ֥י צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ עִוֵּ֑ר וַיַּאַסְרֵ֣הוּ בַֽנְחֻשְׁתַּ֗יִם וַיְבִאֵ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶל֙ בָּבֶ֔לָה וַיִּתְּנֵ֥הוּ בבית בֵֽית הַפְּקֻדֹּ֖ת עַד י֥וֹם מוֹתֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.52.11, byte) — “He put out the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him in fetters, and carried him to Babylon, and put him in prison until the day of his death.” (web:Jer.52.11) — the word for that prison carrying a ketiv/qere pair, detailed below — a notice closed on its own terms rather than by a fresh dated or addressed unit.
row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the siege's dated onset from the capture and sentencing that complete it was rejected because no fresh date, named agent, or formula breaks the chain running from the ninth-year notice to the imprisonment that closes it.
row.literature_type_guess: dated siege narrative ending in the king's capture and sentencing
row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
row.device_notes: Verse 5 carries a mid-narrative duration rather than a fresh dated onset, וַתָּבֹ֥א הָעִ֖יר בַּמָּצ֑וֹר עַ֚ד עַשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.52.5, byte) — “So the city was besieged to the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.” (web:Jer.52.5) — read here on its own bytes as a bridging notice rather than grouped with the chapter's verse-initial date frames; it continues the siege the dated onset above opens rather than starting a fresh one. A ketiv/qere pair stands over the word for Zedekiah's prison at oshb:Jer.52.11 (single-witness WLC): the consonantal text doubles a letter, בבית, against the received בֵֽית, a variant this splice does not otherwise engage. Nebuchadnezzar's name recurs here in its resh-family spelling, matching the spelling this chapter uses at its four other occurrences of the name (sweep: 5 verses).

prev_row.boundary_rationale: This span opens the appendix on Zedekiah's own regnal notice, a bare age-at-accession formula rather than any of the dated frames further into this chapter: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַחַ֤ת שָׁנָה֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וְאַחַ֤ת עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ חמיטל חֲמוּטַ֥ל בַּֽת יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מִלִּבְנָֽה (oshb:Jer.52.1, byte; a ketiv/qere pair sits over the mother's name here, detailed below), matching “Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign. He reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.” (web:Jer.52.1). A regnal evaluation follows in its own verse, וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוֹיָקִֽים (oshb:Jer.52.2, byte) — “He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.” (web:Jer.52.2) — before the span closes on the rebellion report that sets the chapter's crisis in motion, כִּ֣י עַל אַ֣ף יְהוָ֗ה הָֽיְתָה֙ בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה עַד הִשְׁלִיכ֥וֹ אוֹתָ֖ם מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו וַיִּמְרֹ֥ד צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל (oshb:Jer.52.3, byte), matching “For through Yahweh’s anger this happened in Jerusalem and Judah, until he had cast them out from his presence. Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.” (web:Jer.52.3). A paseq stands in this closing verse, oshb:Jer.52.3 (single-witness WLC; seg layer; a bare count, position not recorded). No fresh dating notice interrupts the chain from the accession formula to the rebellion report, so the three verses stay one span.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this opening span through the siege's dated onset that follows was rejected because the accession formula, the regnal evaluation, and the rebellion report form a closed backstory unit before any fresh dated action begins.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: regnal accession notice with evaluation and rebellion report
prev_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
prev_row.device_notes: The queen mother's name carries a ketiv/qere pair at oshb:Jer.52.1 (single-witness WLC): the consonantal text reads חמיטל where the received reading is חֲמוּטַ֥ל, the two forms differing in the letter standing for the name's internal vowel. Zedekiah's name recurs six times across this chapter (1, 3, 5, 8, 10, 11), and in this span it stands twice, at oshb:Jer.52.1 and oshb:Jer.52.3, both times in the long tsidqiyahu spelling (sweep: 6 verses) rather than the short tsidqiyah form the book attests elsewhere. items.question: CWO-5 POLICY RULING (boss-decidable; census direction (c)): the signal-field contract does not say whether a declared closure key may name a device outside the unit's own span. Ten units declare the closure key; six end on a verse carrying none of the book's 162 neum tokens. Enumerate the declaring rows deterministically from the frozen corpus (sweep observed_substrate_signals for the closure-classed key), then rule ONE scope policy: (i) a closure key must be attested in the unit's own span (bind-or-drop, per the P09-002 cure shape), or (ii) qualified out-of-span closure keys are permitted with mandatory disclosure. Name the policy, the exact consequence rows, and the cure test each must pass.

P09-002.challenge_claim: The unit registers a closure signal that its own close does not carry: the closing verse carries 0 neum tokens, and the 2 tokens inside the span both sit mid-verse, so the declared signal has nothing in this span's bytes to rest on.
P09-002.grounds: The byte facts hold exactly. The close reads וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֥י לָהֶ֛ם כְּפָעֳלָ֖ם וּכְמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.25.14, byte tier) and carries none of the formula -- the 162-verse inventory does not list it -- and the two in-span tokens at 25:9 and 25:12 both sit mid-verse and neither closes anything. What the framing overstates is that the signal has nothing to rest on. It rests on the front seam one verse before the span: 25:7 carries נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.25.7, byte tier) and 25:8 opens verse-initially on לָכֵ֕ן כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת (oshb:Jer.25.8, byte tier), a fresh tier-1 onset -- which is precisely the condition under which the ruled treatment lets that formula do closure work, and it is the pairing the boundary rationale itself names. Corrected finding: not a baseless key but an unscoped one, reading as a claim about this unit's own close where the bytes give nothing. Severity holds at low.
P09-002.remedy: Either bind the closure key to the seam it rests on by qualifying it as a front-seam signal, or drop it and let the koh-amar onset key carry the seam alone; in boundary_rationale, state that the closing verse carries no closure formula, so the close rests on the recompense clause completing the sentence begun at 25:8. Cure test: every declared closure signal must be present in the verse it is claimed of -- the test the original failed was a closure key whose only support lies outside the span. For consolidation: this is a corpus_wide_orders candidate rather than a one-unit fix. Ten units declare that closure key and six of them end on a verse carrying none of the 162, and the signal-field contract does not say whether a key may name a device outside the unit's own span; one order should settle the scope question rather than six independent guesses.

row.boundary_rationale: “Therefore Yahweh of Armies says” (web:Jer.25.8) turns on לָכֵ֕ן כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת (oshb:Jer.25.8, byte tier) -- a pivot into a fresh declaration of consequence (the Babylonian invasion, the seventy-year servitude, and Babylon's own eventual reckoning) after the retrospective just closed, though the speaker is Yahweh in both the neum of 25:7 and the koh-amar here, so the seam rests more on the shift from recalling past warnings to pronouncing a dated sentence than on a clean change of who is speaking. The unit runs to 25:14, whose recompense clause closes the sentence begun at 25:8. Midway, the declaration states that Yahweh will bring on the land “even all that is written in this book” (web:Jer.25.13), spliced אֵ֤ת כָּל הַכָּתוּב֙ בַּסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.25.13, byte tier; the verse's opening verb also carries a ketiv/qere note, consulted but not spliced here) -- a self-reference whose scope (this sermon alone, or a wider written collection) this tiling does not resolve, and the row is held at reduced confidence on that account rather than treated as a settled hinge.
row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 25:1-14 as one row spanning the header through the recompense clause was considered: the divine voice does not clearly change between the retrospective and the declaration, so the pivot at 25:8 is a real but not decisive seam, and one fourteen-verse sermon unit would also be defensible.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens on “The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah” (web:Jer.25.1), spliced הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֤ה עַֽל יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ (oshb:Jer.25.1, byte tier) -- a word-event header built on the preposition al (concerning) rather than el (to), doubled again in עַל כָּל עַ֣ם יְהוּדָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.25.1, byte tier), “concerning all the people of Judah.” The header carries its own date stack in the same verse (the fourth year of Jehoiakim, the first year of Nebuchadnezzar) and is followed by a third-person notice of delivery (25:2) before the voice turns first-person at 25:3: “Yahweh’s word has come to me, and I have spoken to you” (web:Jer.25.3), rendering הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י (oshb:Jer.25.3, byte tier) -- Jeremiah's own twenty-three-year retrospective, framing an embedded citation of the call to repentance (25:5-6) that closes “Yet you have not listened to me” (web:Jer.25.7), spliced וְלֹֽא שְׁמַעְתֶּ֥ם אֵלַ֖י נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.25.7, byte tier; the same verse also carries a ketiv/qere note further on, consulted but not spliced here). The row is held to the header-plus-retrospective material because the pivot at 25:8 turns from recounting past warnings to a fresh declaration of consequence.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating 25:1-2 as a bare superscription, separate from the first-person retrospective that follows, was considered and set aside: the retrospective in 25:3-7 carries the row's substance and no addressee shift separates the header from the twenty-three-year account it introduces.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A private commission opens the row: “Take this cup of the wine of wrath from my hand” (web:Jer.25.15), spliced קַ֠ח אֶת כּ֨וֹס הַיַּ֧יִן הַחֵמָ֛ה הַזֹּ֖את מִיָּדִ֑י (oshb:Jer.25.15, byte tier) -- Yahweh, the God of Israel, addressing Jeremiah directly (“to me”), a scene shift from the dated declaration just closed. Jeremiah's own report of compliance follows, “Then I took the cup at Yahweh’s hand” (web:Jer.25.17), rendering וָאֶקַּ֥ח אֶת הַכּ֖וֹס מִיַּ֣ד יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.25.17, byte tier), and the roster of nations made to drink (25:18-26) runs into a command that keeps the same audience, “You shall tell them, ‘Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says…” (web:Jer.25.27), spliced וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֡ם כֹּֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.25.27, byte tier) -- a discourse imperative addressed to the nations already given the cup rather than a new audience, so the row treats it as the act's own enforcement clause rather than a fresh unit. The whole complex closes at 25:29's declaration that Yahweh is calling for a sword against the earth. Whether this cup vision anticipates the later nations material or stands as this sermon's own close is left open here, and the row is held at reduced confidence on that account.
